svg.title: A toddler continues to refuse a necessary medication after every other approach has been tried. What is the appropriate last resort?
svg.desc: When a medication is necessary, brief gentle holding may be needed — with the child reassured it is not a punishment, positioned to avoid choking, and given as much control as possible. The parent is often the best person to give it. Using visitors as leverage is coercion, not care.

g.text: STUDY HUB / QUESTION MAP
Intro to Pediatric Nursing
Read the situation
A toddler continues to refuse a necessary
medication after every other approach has
been tried. What is the appropriate last
resort?
What fits here
Use gentle physical holding, reassuring
the child it is not a punishment and
guarding against aspiration
Why it fits
When a medication is necessary, brief
gentle holding may be needed — with the
child reassured it is not a punishment,
positioned to avoid choking, and given as
much control as possible. The parent is
often the best person to give it. Using
visitors as leverage is coercion, not
care.
